meta.name: SWARM
meta.note: Single source of truth for every number shown on the site. Values come from the SWARM mainnet launch manifest (rendered 2026-10-02T15:42:42Z). Edit here, then mirror the same values in the static HTML fallbacks (see README.md).

status.ribbon: SWARM mainnet is live · public mining opens 1 November 2026.
status.detail: SWARM mainnet has been live since 2 October 2026, 15:42 UTC. The genesis block holds no spendable coins; every SWM that exists has been mined. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project's own machines mine; for the next 24 hours the people on the waiting list can mine too, and from 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC mining is open to everyone.

closedStart.note: The first 30 days of the chain: 29 days in which only the project mines (figures from 29 days at the 75-second target: 33,408 blocks x 6.25 SWM = 208,800 SWM, 0.9943% of 20,999,987.3152), then 24 hours of early access for the waiting list (owner decision 2026-10-03). untilUtc is the public opening and drives the countdown.
closedStart.split: 80% to the project's mining wallet, 20% to the three funds
closedStart.summary: Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project's own machines can mine: in those 29 days about 33,408 blocks are produced, about 208,800 SWM (80% to the project's mining wallet, 20% to the three funds), about 0.99% of the cap. From then until 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC the people on the waiting list can mine too; from that moment mining is open to everyone and the node software will be published on this site. Why: the infrastructure around the coin, liquidity pools included, needs coins before public mining begins; the aim is an orderly, predictable start.
closedStart.openedNote: Stays false until public mining has actually opened. Set it to true only together with available node rows (product "node") in data/downloads.json and a page at downloadPath: /waitlist then shows the download instead of the sign-up form, and tools/build_pages.py refuses to build the open state without such a row.

chain.lineage: Proven open-source code with consensus rules and cryptography left unmodified.

genesis.note: Read from the SWARM mainnet launch manifest of 2 October 2026 (manifest.json sha256 40794956b04e958cdfef2a18fdda628355287767c3f8dc6eb20c1e7ecb387325). The baseline-miner payout address is operational, not consensus, and is deliberately not listed.
genesis.custody: Each script is controlled by three key shares generated offline at the launch key ceremony and held under the custody policy published with the launch manifest; two of the three are needed to spend.

rewardSplit.label: Fixed in the genesis rules for the whole emission schedule. Paid block by block as part of each block reward — not a premine.
rewardSplit.appliesFor: The whole emission schedule. Every halving reduces all four amounts proportionally, keeping the same 80 / 8 / 4 / 8 structure, until block rewards reach zero.
rewardSplit.destinations: Each allocation is paid automatically to its predefined destination address. Destinations can only be changed through a formal protocol upgrade; the percentages themselves cannot be changed.

shares.name: Miner
shares.desc: Paid to the forager who found the block.

shares.name: Core Development
shares.desc: Funds work on the node, indexer and wallet.

shares.name: Grants & Ecosystem
shares.desc: Funds tooling, documentation and community work.

shares.name: Community & Development Reserve
shares.desc: Set aside for the community and for future development. How it is governed and spent will be defined separately and published before mainnet launches.

lifetimeTotals.note: Amounts are exact to the smallest unit for the first seven eras (about 28 years). After that the inherited rounding rule rounds each allocation down to a whole unit and the miner receives the remainder, which is why the lifetime miner share is fractionally above 80%.

emission.note: Cumulative supply over the first 20 years, derived from block time, block reward and halving interval.

deliveries.note: What has actually shipped, what is being built now, and what is only planned. Rendered on /roadmap. Rules: 'live' means the public can use it today and the date is the day it became public; 'in-development' means work has started and there is no date; 'planned' means it has not started and gets neither a date nor a promise.

items.name: Public testnet
items.detail: The public SWARM test network, mined in the open. It is still running, still published, and its coins have no value.

items.name: SWARM mainnet
items.detail: Live since 15:42 UTC. The genesis block holds no spendable coins; every SWM that exists has been mined. Closed start: until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project's own machines mine, about 33,408 blocks and about 208,800 SWM (80% to the project's mining wallet, 20% to the three funds); the people on the waiting list follow 24 hours before public mining opens on 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC.

items.name: Wallet SDK, swarm-sdk-mainnet-1
items.detail: The light-wallet SDK carrying the SWARM mainnet network definition, published so other wallets can be built against the same chain.

items.name: SWARM Messenger for Windows, Linux and macOS
items.detail: The first public desktop release, 0.1.0: end-to-end encrypted messaging between SWARM wallets on SWARM’s own server, sign-in with the 24 words instead of a phone number, usernames, photos and files, the wallet inside the app and payments inside a chat. Unsigned builds; a first release.

items.name: SWARM Browser for Windows, pre-release
items.detail: Build 153.0.8010.52-4 (three builds on the first day): a Windows browser built on Chromium 153 from the ungoogled-chromium code base, with Google’s services removed, privacy defaults switched on and the SWARM wallet built in; a SWARM welcome page, SWARM Start on every new tab, the SWARM Navigator side panel, SWARM’s own icons and colours, DuckDuckGo as the default search. Unsigned; no automatic updates yet. Its built-in wallet no longer connects to the network until the next build; the browser itself works.

items.name: SWARM Wallet for Android
items.detail: SWARM Wallet 0.1.0-mainnet.10 is the current version for Windows, macOS and Linux. Earlier versions (desktop 0.1.0-mainnet.9 and older, Android 0.2.0-mainnet.4) no longer connect to the network; the Android version that does is being prepared.

items.name: Mobile wallets in the app stores
items.detail: The Android wallet is a direct APK you install yourself; the published APK (0.2.0-mainnet.4) no longer connects to the network. The Google Play listing and the iPhone build are being prepared.

items.name: SWARM Market
items.detail: A marketplace where merchants list what they sell and buyers pay in SWM, shielded by default and without custody. Non-custodial invoices come first; escrow, multisignature and dispute handling need their own protocol and operational review before any of it ships.

items.name: A wider operator network
items.detail: More full nodes in more places, starting with machines the project runs itself and opening out from there. The Swarm map shows the cities whose operators asked to be listed.

items.name: A second seed node
items.detail: One seed node is one failure domain. A second seed in a different network and a different provider removes the single point that new nodes currently bootstrap from.

items.name: Custody tooling for the three funds
items.detail: The 2-of-3 signing procedure for the published fund addresses has been exercised end to end. The tooling and the written policy around it are being finished so the process is repeatable and reviewable, not improvised.

items.name: An independent security review
items.detail: A review of the code as it was launched, by people who did not write it. Its findings will be published, including the ones that are uncomfortable.

items.name: A pool protocol for miners
items.detail: Today every miner is solo. A pool needs a work-distribution protocol, share accounting and an answer to who holds rewards before they are paid out — that last part needs review before it exists.

items.name: Integrations in other software
items.detail: Making SWM reachable from software the project does not write. Nothing is agreed and nothing is announced.

items.name: The rest of the privacy browser
items.detail: What the Windows pre-release does not do yet: pay a site from the address bar, block ads and trackers, warn about phishing sites, and run on macOS and Linux. Its rewards page pays nothing, and nothing about rewards is promised.

items.name: Private messaging on phones, groups and calls
items.detail: The desktop messenger is out. Next: the Android and iPhone apps, groups, and voice and video calls.
